newsitem.title: ZAIRE: February referendum on Zaire constitution.
newsitem.headline: February referendum on Zaire constitution.

text.p: Zaire's president, Mobutu Sese Seko, has promulgated a law clearing the way for the holding of a referendum on a federal constitution in February, state radio reported on Monday.
The radio described the move as a "fillip" for the chaotic and war-ravaged Central African nation's much-delayed democratic transition. No date has been set for the poll.
Under the transition, agreed after Mobutu bowed to domestic and foreign pressure for reform in 1990, elections must now be held by May 1997.
But sceptics doubt the ability of the central authorities, who have lost a swath of territory in the east to Tutsi-led rebels, to organise polls within the deadline.
Zaire's transitional parliament approved a federal constitution in October. It envisages cutting the country into 26 provinces, instead of the 11 at present.
The main opposition led by Etienne Tshisekedi oppposes the proposed constitution. Supporters of Mobutu, who seized power in 1965, hold a majority in the transitional parliament.
